article: Display Japanese text in egui using a bundled font
scope: Compared the complete Japanese article and twelve translations, eframe template structure, egui font API, supported font format, Japanese font source/license, code paths, dates, and image reference.
findings: Removed duplicate future date; retained 2023-04-01 and set lastmod to 2026-11-24.
Replaced Meiryo.ttc because egui documents .ttf and .otf font data, and updated font_data insertion to the current Arc<FontData> API.
Switched to Noto Sans JP variable TTF from Google Fonts and described where to place the file relative to src/app.rs.
Updated the initialization location to TemplateApp::new in the current eframe template and retained proportional-font priority.
Added the SIL Open Font License redistribution note and official API/font references.

post/eguiで日本語を表示する方法/index.en.md.source: post/eguiで日本語を表示する方法/index.md
post/eguiで日本語を表示する方法/index.en.md.summary: Compared the complete Japanese article and twelve translations with current egui, eframe-template, and Google Fonts documentation. Replaced the unsupported Windows TTC example and outdated FontData insertion with a current Arc-based registration example using Noto Sans JP TTF.

meaning.note: Compared the goal (render Japanese glyphs), font registration, font-family priority, current eframe initialization hook, and cross-platform assumptions.

terminology.note: Verified egui FontDefinitions, FontData, Arc, Proportional family, eframe CreationContext, Noto Sans JP, TTF, and SIL Open Font License.

code.note: Updated font_data insertion to Arc<FontData>, selected a supported .ttf file, kept the filename path relative to src/app.rs, and applied the font with cc.egui_ctx.set_fonts.

links.note: Added current eframe template, egui API, Google Fonts file metadata, and font license references; checked the existing image reference.

limitations: AI-assisted review; no human or native-speaker certification.
The example assumes the reader downloads the named Noto Sans JP TTF into assets/fonts/ and includes that file in the project; the font is not bundled with the article.
If redistributing the font, include and follow the SIL Open Font License.
